judged_text: remove_member mutates membership through the raw association (group.users.delete(user_id)) while its sibling add_members routes through the model API Group#add, even though the code this same PR removes used group.remove(user) for deletion. The next change that adds bookkeeping to Group#remove (counter maintenance, user/flair cache invalidation) is applied to the model method but silently skipped by remove_member's direct association delete, so removals leave stale state; maintainers of this controller must remember to update two divergent mutation paths.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the diff shows membership removal is done via the raw association `group.users.delete(user_id)` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb), while additions in `add_members` go through `group.add(user)`. The same PR removed prior code paths that used `group.remove(user)` for deletions (the deleted `update_patch` method). This creates divergent mutation APIs in the controller, which is a concrete maintainability/architecture concern: any behavior encapsulated in `Group#remove` (callbacks, side effects) would not run for this new endpoint. The diff alone does not prove a current functional bug (no bookkeeping logic is shown), but it is a specific, grounded issue introduced by this change.
